title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§45 of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck studies the profinite group \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}, which he identifies with SL(2,Z)^ (the profinite completion of SL(2,Z), i.e. a version of \hat\pi_1 of the moduli orbifold M_{1,1}). It is an extension of \mathfrak S_3 = SL(2,Z/2) by \Pi_{0,3}^ (essentially the completed Γ(2), related to \hat\pi_1(P^1-{0,1,∞})). M̃_{0,3} is the group of 'automorphismes à lacets' of \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} that induce the trivial outer action on \mathfrak S_3. These are automorphisms respecting the conjugacy classes of the distinguished loops, i.e. a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type condition. There is an extension 1 → Inn → M̃_{0,3} → Ñ_{0,3} → 1. Ñ_{0,3} is the corresponding outer group, called Γ̃, which contains Γ_Q. The extension is split by the subgroup Γ̃_σ of automorphisms commuting with a fixed element σ_0. Since the centre is ±1 there is a subtlety; σ_0 is a distinguished elliptic element.

This page:
(3) M̃_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ ⋊ Γ̃_σ, a semidirect product.
(4) φ'_0 : SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ) is the canonical map (congruence quotient), landing in a subgroup GL(2,Ẑ)'.
(5) φ'_σ : Γ̃_σ → GL(2,Ẑ)' sends u to μ(tσ_∞ + u)τ_∞^{α} = μ [[u, εt], [−t, εu]]. Here:
- t, u ∈ Ẑ, μ ∈ Ẑ^*, ε = (−1)^α, and these quantities are attached to u in the previous §§.
- σ_∞ has square −1 (order 4), so tσ_∞ + u ranges over the 'Gaussian' Cartan Ẑ[σ_∞] ≅ Ẑ[i].
- τ_∞ is an involution normalising this Cartan, acting like complex conjugation.
So φ'_σ takes values in the normaliser of the Cartan Ẑ[i]^* in GL_2(Ẑ). The determinant is μ²ε(u²+t²).
(6)-(7) φ' : M̃_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)' is defined by φ'(a·u) = φ'_0(a)φ'_σ(u).

The next page states the theorem that φ' is a group homomorphism. Since φ'_0 is a homomorphism, this reduces to two facts:
- φ'_σ is a homomorphism. This is proved via cocycle relations for the auxiliary quantities g, h, f.
- The compatibility φ'_0(u(a)) = φ'_σ(u)φ'_0(a)φ'_σ(u)^{-1} holds. This holds by construction (earlier formulas (67), (68), (77)).

Purpose: build a 'linear representation' of the whole Teichmüller-type group M̃_{0,3} (and hence of Γ̃) into GL_2(Ẑ). This extends the congruence representation of SL(2,Z)^ and leads to the extension Ñ_{1,1} of Γ̃ by SL(2,Z)^. Arithmetically it mimics the Galois action of Γ_Q on the Tate module of an elliptic curve with CM by Z[i] (j = 1728, e.g. y² = x³ − x). That action lands exactly in the normaliser of Ẑ[i]^* in GL_2(Ẑ), with τ acting as complex conjugation, and the σ-fixed point corresponds to the elliptic point i of M_{1,1}.
errors: The exponent of τ_∞ written as ε cannot be right: τ_∞ is an involution, so τ_∞^{±1} = τ_∞. To get μ[[u, εt], [−t, εu]] one needs τ_∞^{α} with α ∈ Z/2 and τ_∞ = diag(1, −1) up to convention. The next page writes τ_∞^{ξ}, again an exponent slip.

Minor: (7) defines φ' only through a chosen decomposition a·u. This is fine because (3) is a semidirect product decomposition, but whether φ' is a homomorphism is precisely the content of the following theorem, not automatic.

The identification \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ and the target 'GL(2,Ẑ)′' (prime = some subgroup defined earlier) are not self-explanatory on this page. Exact conventions (e.g. the role of −1, or the determinant condition) cannot be checked from the page alone.

ideas.what: Group of 'loop-preserving' automorphisms of the profinite completion of SL(2,Z) (≈ \hat\pi_1 of M_{1,1}) trivial on S_3, with a canonical splitting by the stabiliser of an elliptic element
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on \hat\pi_1(M_{1,1}) / GT-type automorphism groups of SL(2,Z)^
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto for genus 1 / M_{1,1}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and SL(2,Z)^; this detailed construction is in the unpublished Longue Marche follow-up notes

ideas.what: Homomorphism from the whole automorphism group M̃_{0,3} = SL(2,Z)^ ⋊ Γ̃_σ to GL_2(Ẑ), extending the congruence map, with Γ̃_σ landing in the normaliser of the Gaussian Cartan Ẑ[i]^*
ideas.modern_name: Extension of a GT-type group action to a 'CM Tate module' representation (analogue of Galois on T(E) for E with CM by Z[i]); related to Ihara–Anderson Jacobi-sum characters on GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (universal power series for Jacobi sums, 1986), Anderson; for GT-analogues partly Ihara, Nakamura

ideas.what: Reduction of the homomorphism property to cocycle relations for the auxiliary invariants (g, h, f) of each automorphism (next page)

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs, purely combinatorially from the group of 'loop-preserving' automorphisms (a GT-like group), a representation into the normaliser of the Cartan Ẑ[i]^* ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ in GL_2(Ẑ). On Γ_Q it should restrict to the Galois action on the Tate module of the j = 1728 CM elliptic curve. This implicitly defines a Z[i]-valued 'Hecke character' on the whole Teichmüller-type group Γ̃. The literature has such things via Ihara's Jacobi-sum power series, but an explicit GL_2(Ẑ)-valued homomorphism of the full extension SL(2,Z)^ ⋊ Γ̃_σ, built from the stabiliser of an elliptic point, is not a standard published object as far as I know.
missed.quote: φ'_σ : Γ̃_σ → Gl(2,Ẑ)' , u ↦ μ(tσ_∞ + u)τ_∞^ε = μ( u εt ; −t εu )
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests that CM-type Galois representations (j = 1728, and perhaps j = 0 via the order-6 elliptic point) extend to GT-hat or its genus-1 variants in a canonical way. This links GT theory with CM/Jacobi-sum characters and with the structure of GT acting on \hat\pi_1(M_{1,1}) at its elliptic points.

missed.claim: The construction is aimed at the extension Ñ_{1,1} of Γ̃ by SL(2,Z)^ (a genus-1 analogue of the GT extension), whose properties are developed only in these notes.
missed.quote: construction de l'extension Ñ_{1,1} de Γ̃ par Sl(2,Z)^ (section title, previous page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a genus-one GT-type extension defined via stabilisers of elliptic points. It could be compared with the genus-one GT groups of Hain–Matsumoto and Enriquez (elliptic associators).

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up an explicit homomorphism from a GT-like automorphism group of SL(2,Z)^ into the normaliser of the Gaussian Cartan in GL_2(Ẑ), mimicking the CM elliptic curve at j = 1728. GT actions on M_{1,1} are known, but this specific CM-flavoured linear representation of the whole group is not a standard literature object, so it is a notable unpublished detail. It is not clearly a dramatic new result.
transcription_corrections: The group written Π̃_σ is Γ̃_σ (double-struck/tilde Gamma), consistent with the next page's Γ̃_σ.
Equation (5): exponent of τ_∞ should be read as α (or a symbol with values in Z/2); the manuscript shows ε, which is a slip.
'pour indiquer la dépendance par à u' should read 'pour indiquer la dépendance par r[apport] à u'.
In (3) the underbrace 'Sl(2,Z)^' identifies \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}; the M̃_{0,3} tilde is over the whole symbol.
The crossed-out line above the 'où' list reads roughly 't, u, α_2 ...' with 'ε_2 ε_∞' inserted; the final list is t, u ∈ Ẑ, μ ∈ Ẑ^*, ε = ε_2 ∈ {±1}, α = α_2 ∈ Z/2Z.
